name: Easy Moving Permits
description: Online platform to apply for and manage moving / street / dumpster / scaffolding parking permits across cities — transparent pricing including city fees + service charge; charged per application via Stripe.

mentions.evidence: ~$2.0k L30, MRR $0 / no active subscriptions (transaction model), ~$24.4k all-time, founded Nov 2025, US. Last sync Sep 30, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Government-process UX for one city → expand city-by-city; service fee on top of municipal fees.

whyItPrints: Civic permit glue. Movers and residents will pay to not get towed. Transaction model, not seats — same energy as MyCater's "take a cut of the inevitable spend."
whyThisMatters:
Movers use Easy Moving Permits when the truck needs the curb. Enter the address, pick the date, and they file the permit, post the no-parking signs, and send a photo before moving day. Your card isn't charged until the permit is approved. You see the city fee and the lead time before you pay.

A moving permit covers a truck or a container. A street permit covers construction, a dumpster, filming, or scaffolding. Boston is one city for that street permit. You can estimate the cost, and you can check whether your address is served. Without the permit you're looking at tickets, no reserved spot, a possible tow, and overtime if the crew is hauling from down the block. An office manager at a Massachusetts moving company wrote about fast replies and photos of the posted signs.

You pay per application. City fee and service charge, one checkout. No monthly seat. The company started in the US in November 2025. The product is the paperwork and the signs.
